content.overview: Section 30 requires that every advertisement of a prospectus must specify the contents of the memorandum as regards objects, liability of members, amount of share capital, the names of the signatories to the memorandum and the number of shares subscribed for by them, and the capital structure of the company.
content.glance: Prospectus advertisements must state specified memorandum particulars and capital structure; the rule is disclosure-focused and operates alongside the full prospectus regime.
content.study: Where any advertisement of a prospectus of a company is published in any manner, the advertisement must specify the contents of the memorandum as regards the objects, the liability of members, the amount of share capital of the company, the names of the signatories to the memorandum and the number of shares subscribed for by them, and the capital structure of the company. The provision ensures that even a short advertisement carries core constitutional and capital information. It does not replace the full prospectus under s. 26. Current-law framing: identify a published advertisement of a prospectus; check the mandatory memorandum and capital disclosures.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Publication of an advertisement of a prospectus in any manner engages s. 30.

sections.heading: Mandatory Particulars
sections.body: The advertisement must state memorandum objects, member liability, share capital, memorandum signatories and their subscribed shares, and capital structure.

sections.heading: Relation to Full Prospectus
sections.body: Section 30 is an advertisement disclosure rule; the full prospectus content and filing duties remain under s. 26 and related provisions.

examples.title: Compliant advertisement
examples.body: A company publishes a prospectus advertisement that states the required memorandum and capital-structure particulars. Section 30 is met.

examples.title: Bare promotional ad
examples.body: An advertisement of a prospectus omits objects, capital and signatory details. Section 30 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Does a short advertisement replace the need for a full prospectus?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 30 only regulates what an advertisement of a prospectus must state; the full prospectus regime under s. 26 remains.

distinctions.title: Advertisement of prospectus (s. 30) vs content of prospectus (s. 26)
distinctions.left: Minimum particulars in any published advertisement
distinctions.right: Full statutory content, dating, signing and ROC filing

misconceptions.trap: Any promotional material about an issue is free of statutory content rules.
misconceptions.correction: If it is an advertisement of a prospectus, s. 30 requires specified memorandum and capital particulars.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 30 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify advertisement of a prospectus. II. Check mandatory particulars. III. Distinguish from full s. 26 duties. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Advertisement text; missing particulars if any; relation to prospectus; precise relief.

examTips: Do not treat s. 30 as a substitute for the full prospectus.
